summary: Somtum Der is a casual Sala Daeng restaurant for Isan food, with many styles of som tum alongside grilled meats, fried chicken, soups and sticky rice. Its current 2026 menu has both milder Thai-style papaya salad and more pungent Isan versions with fermented fish, so it can suit diners who want to explore beyond one dish.
whyGo: The menu offers a broad, shareable introduction to regional Isan flavors, from classic Tum Thai to Tum Suo and fermented-fish salads.
Pair papaya salad with sticky rice, grilled pork or fried chicken for a more rounded meal.
The Sala Daeng branch is close to BTS Sala Daeng and MRT Silom, convenient in the Silom area.
bestFor: Diners who enjoy spicy, sour, salty and fermented flavors
Small groups who want to share several dishes
Visitors looking for a relaxed meal near Silom transit
skipIf: You need confirmed allergen separation or a verified mild-food preparation process
You dislike chili, fermented fish, or pungent flavors and do not want to ask about milder options
You need verified step-free access or accessible toilets
duration: Allow about 1–1.5 hours for a meal; this is a planning estimate, and waits may extend it at busy times.
cost: The official 2026 menu lists papaya salads around THB 80–140, with many other dishes in a similar range and some meat dishes higher. Budget roughly THB 300–600 per person for a shared meal, as a planning estimate; prices are subject to 10% service charge and 7% VAT. Confirm the current menu and final bill at the branch.
hours: The official Sala Daeng listing says open daily 11:00–23:00, last order 22:15. Holiday hours may differ.
bestTime: Go for an early lunch or early dinner if you prefer a quieter meal. Ask staff to recommend a spice level and whether a dish contains fermented fish before ordering.
gettingThere: At 5/5 Sala Daeng Road, Silom, Bang Rak. The restaurant lists BTS Sala Daeng Exit 4 and MRT Silom Exit 2; use a live map for the short final walk.
booking: The official website provides a booking link for Sala Daeng. Reserve if visiting with a group or at a peak dinner time; availability and booking terms were not independently checked.
accessibility: The sources reviewed do not describe step-free access, accessible toilets, table layout or accommodation for mobility needs. Contact the restaurant before visiting if these are important.
practicalTips: Order a few dishes to share; the restaurant describes Isan meals as a shared-dish style, often accompanied by sticky rice.
The menu distinguishes Thai-style papaya salad without fermented fish from Isan-style dishes with it; confirm ingredients with staff, especially for allergies.
Chili tolerance varies. Ask whether the kitchen can adjust a dish before ordering; this was not confirmed in published information.
The menu price note adds 10% service charge and 7% VAT.
decemberNotes: No special December 2026 service or event was listed in the sources reviewed. December is a busy Bangkok travel period, so consider booking through the official site and reconfirm holiday hours shortly before visiting.
uncertainties: The official branch page does not specify holiday exceptions; daily listed hours may change around Christmas or New Year.
The meal budget is an estimate from listed 2026 menu prices and sharing portions, not a quoted set price.
